preamble: A velar ejective [kʼ] becomes a uvular implosive [ʛ]: the stop moves back to the uvula and the airstream switches from egressive to ingressive. Konso (Lowland East Cushitic) has no ejectives. Instead it has four implosives, ɓ ɗ ʄ ʛ. Orkaydo (2013: 8) states that ejectives in loanwords become implosives, and that Amharic kʼ systematically gives the uvular ʛ (also cʼ > ʄ, pʼ > ɓ, while tʼ and sʼ become plain t and s). The sources checked here do not say whether native Konso ʛ also continues Proto-Eastern Cushitic *kʼ; closely related Gidole keeps kʼ (Ehret 1991 #92). Separately, Ehret (1991) describes the Dullay and Yaaku reflex of PEC *kʼ, written q, as 'a uvular, but an unusual one, an implosive voiceless stop', i.e. [ʛ̥]. Burji and Gidole keep kʼ in some of the same roots (Ehret #92). The Konso loans have voiced ʛ, but the Dullay and Yaaku sound is voiceless, so the cell's voiced symbol fits it only approximately.
phoneticEffects: Implosivization, Retraction, Airstream Change, Loanword Adaptation
